**Indikator** (Indicator) refers to the quantitative metrics used to measure and evaluate the quality of atrial fibrillation treatment within the Danish healthcare system. As detailed in the 2024 AFDK (Atrieflimren i Danmark) report, these indicators are a core component of the national quality development framework, which aims to ensure uniform, evidence-based, and patient-centered care for a frequent and potentially serious chronic heart disease [^src1]. The broader framework relies on the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database to monitor clinical practices—such as structured patient education—while also acknowledging methodological limitations in national data collection [^src1].

A central decision documented in the 2024 evaluation is the retention of the indicator's performance threshold, with the quality standard officially set at [[50-percent]] [^src1]. This benchmark directly governs how clinical performance is assessed and maintained across Danish hospitals and regions, making it a critical element of the country's healthcare quality infrastructure and cardiology performance monitoring [^src1].
